title: Everything You Need to Track Your Story World
use_cases: Use when visualizing character networks to identify central or isolated figures
Implement when automating the creation of character bios and world lore from manuscript content
Configure when tracking character appearances and scene locations across a long-form manuscript
Use when mapping geographical locations and travel routes for consistent story setting
Configure when generating complex genealogical charts or family trees automatically
Use when managing character aliases to ensure consistent identity tracking across chapters
content:
🕸

Force-directed graph showing character connections. Hover to see details, drag to rearrange. Node size reflects how connected each character is.

🔍

AI scans your scenes and automatically finds which characters appear together. No manual tagging required — your codex stays up to date as you write.

✨

One click generates detailed descriptions from your story content. Fill out character bios, location details, and item lore without leaving the editor.

📍

See exactly which scenes each character appears in. Click to jump directly to that scene. Track presence across your entire manuscript at a glance.

📈

Track how characters evolve across the story with AI-generated progression summaries. See their arc from first appearance to final scene.

🏷

Automatically split names into searchable aliases for better detection. "Lord Alistair Blackwood" becomes searchable as "Alistair," "Blackwood," and "Lord Blackwood."

🗺

Drag every place onto an interactive map. Upload your own atlas or use the built-in grid. Distances, regions, and travel routes — all visual.

👪

Auto-built from typed relationships. Spouse, sibling, parent, lover — the tree assembles itself across generations with multiple themes and layouts.

✨

One prompt, full codex. Describe your setting and the AI seeds characters, places, factions, and items with consistent lore and relationships.
